title: Determining Core-Shell Colloidal Quantum Dot Structures from Various Synthesis Methods Using Cryo-STEM
content: III–V compounds (e.g., GaAs, InGaAs) are essential semiconductors due to their direct band gaps and outstanding electronic properties [1]. Advances in colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) now offer precise control over size and shape, resulting in improved tunability, narrower emissions, and higher photoluminescence yields than epitaxial dots [2]. Their solution processability and relatively low refractive index compared to the bulk material enhance photon extraction, paving the way for QLEDs that typically use only a few layers of core–shell CQDs for bright emission and efficient charge injection [3].
